description: In 1905 and 1915, Einstein changed our idea of ​​space, time and gravity. And without its calculations, your GPS would be wrong by several kilometers.

hero.hook: Time is not a universal clock. And gravity is not an invisible string.

blocks.text: In **1905** and **1915**, **Albert Einstein** published two theories that shook up physics. Until then, we mainly followed : time flowed the same way for everyone, everywhere. [[Newton]]

Einstein shows that space and time are linked, and that gravity can be understood as a curvature of this tissue. These ideas explain the  and the . They also correct your phone's GPS every day. [[black holes]] [[Big Bang]]

**special relativity** is based on two simple ideas. The laws of nature are the same for everyone who moves at a constant speed. And the speed of light in a vacuum, **about 300,000 km/s**, is the same for everyone, whether we are approaching it or moving away from it.

blocks.caption: Albert Einstein, author of the theory of relativity.

blocks.text: For light to always keep the same speed, time must adjust. It's : the faster an object goes, the slower time passes for it compared to someone at rest. This is not an illusion. **atomic clocks**, instruments that measure time with extreme precision, measured it. [[Time dilation]]

Einstein also draws : mass is a very concentrated form of energy. As **c**, the speed of light, is enormous, a very small mass can release colossal energy. It is a pillar of , the study of atomic nuclei and their reactions. [[E=mc²]] [[nuclear physics]]
In 1905, Einstein was not a university professor. He works as an examiner at the patent office in Bern, Switzerland.

Ten years later, Einstein published the **general relativity**. Newton saw gravity as an invisible force pulling masses toward each other. Einstein offers another image: **space-time**, space and time united in a single fabric, forms a flexible fabric.

A heavy mass, like the Sun, hollows out this tissue. Imagine a bowling ball on a trampoline. A ball thrown next to it does not go straight: it follows the hollow. Likewise, the Earth orbits because it follows the curvature created by the Sun.

Even light follows these curves. In **1919**, the British astronomer **Arthur Eddington** verified it during an eclipse: the apparent position of stars behind the Sun is slightly shifted. Einstein becomes famous overnight.

GPS satellites rotate at approximately **14,000 km/h**, at **20,000 km** altitude. To locate yourself to the nearest meter, their clocks must remain synchronized with those on the ground. But two relativistic effects operate at the same time.

Because of their speed, time passes a little more slowly, an effect of special relativity: approximately **7 microseconds** delay per day. Because of the weaker gravity at altitude, time passes a little faster there, an effect of general relativity: approximately **45 microseconds** in advance.
Without relativistic corrections, the GPS position error could reach approximately **11 km** per day.
The result is a net advance of approximately **38 microseconds** per day. It seems tiny. At the speed of light, this is already huge for navigation.

General relativity predicts black holes: regions where the curvature is so strong that even light no longer comes out. Einstein doubted their real existence. The , observation of the sky in radio waves, and recent images have confirmed them. [[radio astronomy]]

In **1916**, he also predicted **gravitational waves**: ripples in space-time produced by cosmic catastrophes, such as the merger of two black holes. We have to wait for **2015** and the **LIGO** observatory, a ground detector sensitive to space vibrations, to detect them.

Finally, these equations open the way to an expanding universe, the basis of the Big Bang model. Einstein had first added a cosmological constant****, a mathematical term for forcing a fixed universe. Hubble's observations later convinced him otherwise.
**E=mc²** links mass and energy. General relativity says that gravity bends space-time. Without these corrections, your GPS would be several kilometers wrong every day.
